00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, we really appreciate the time, quick roll call, i'm maya c from redwood and carlos is on the se side, uh could we just go around?
00:08 Liam: yeah liam here, head of ml at aurora, thanks for doing this, we've been looking at cost reduction and latency improvements for customer support ai flows.
00:15 Priya: priya, platform eng, i'll be primary on infra and networking questions.
00:18 Ethan: ethan here, i'll listen for ops + security implications.
00:22 Carlos: great, thanks. quick agenda: current architecture, batching basics, prefix vs kv cache, cost modeling, security notes, then next steps. sound good?
00:30 Liam: yep

02:05 Carlos: can you share current stack really quick? we grabbed some pre-call notes but want to confirm traffic shape and token sizes.
02:12 Liam: sure, we're currently on openai API for generation, across chat endpoints. average request is about 1.2k tokens in the happy path (customer message + context) but most of the time our context replays common history bits so the effective unique tokens are lower. we do about 80 reqs/sec at peak, spiky, daily 1M requests.
02:29 Maya: ok that helps, and retention/security? you mentioned regulatory customers.
02:33 Priya: yes—data residency and audit logs are important. we need KMS integration, SOC2, and the ability to run in a VPC or on-prem for 1-2 of our enterprise clients.

04:10 Carlos: perfect. so on batching — high level — Redwood does dynamic batching in the runtime; we group requests to improve GPU utilization while keeping latency SLOs. two knobs to call out: max batch size and max latency window (ms). also prefix batching where we batch identical prefixes to exploit kv cache.
04:30 Liam: when you say kv cache, are we talking about prefix caching at the token/key-value level, like reusing KV cache across similar prompts?
04:36 Carlos: exactly, kv cache is the attention key/value cache. for requests that share early tokens (prefix), we can avoid recomputing the prefix and only run the suffix, so compute drops a lot. we also do prefix-indexing to find cache hits at runtime.

07:20 Priya: what hit-rate can we expect? our sessions often reuse the first ~150 tokens for system+persona.
07:25 Carlos: typical hit-rates in our customer base range 25-70% depending on how templated the prompts are. with heavy templating (support flows, known id fields) you can see 50-70%. with looser natural prompts it may be 20-30%.
07:42 Maya: we made a quick cost model for your profile. using your 80 rps peak and 1.2k token average, we estimate base per-token compute cost on hosted model X is about $0.000012/token. with batching + cache you can reduce effective tokens computed per request to ~300 tokens on average (assuming 60% cache hit on 900-token prefix), so per-request cost falls ~3-4x.
07:58 Liam: can you run that again slower — the 900-token prefix number? our average was 1.2k total, so are you splitting system+prompt+history into a 900 prefix and 300 suffix?
08:05 Carlos: yes that's a working assumption: many customers place most static context and system instructions at the front; we assume 900 tokens are reusable. the cache hit reduces the effective compute to only the last 300 tokens per request on hit. on miss you still run full 1.2k. overall expected computed tokens = hit_rate * suffix + (1 - hit_rate) * full. so with 60% hit and suffix 300: 0.6*300 + 0.4*1200 = 540 tokens computed average vs 1200 baseline.
08:35 Priya: ok that math makes sense. where does batching help then?
08:38 Carlos: batching primarily raises GPU throughput; it reduces per-token kernel overhead and can improve throughput-per-GPU by 1.6-2.5x depending on model/hardware. so caching reduces tokens computed, batching reduces cost per computed token. combined effect multiplies.

11:50 Ethan: curious about latency tradeoffs — can we keep p95 under 300ms? our SLAs call for under 350ms p95 in region.
11:58 Carlos: yes; with dynamic batching tuned (max wait 10ms, max batch size tuned to p95 target) and prefix cache hits that avoid long autoregressive compute, customers often meet sub-300ms p95 on dedicated infra. Hosted may have slightly higher tail depending on region and load, but we offer Dedicated with latency SLAs.
12:15 Maya: note — we can set routing policy so enterprise tier goes to Dedicated pool to guarantee latency and hosted for non-critical routes.

14:20 Liam: ok show me a sample configuration you recommend.
14:25 Carlos: sure — recommended starting config for Aurora:
- max_batch_size: 64
- max_queue_ms: 8-12 (start 10ms)
- per-route cache policy: prefix-ttl 24h, cache-indexing enabled, max-kv-size trimmed to 512MB per model instance
- cold-start fallback: if cache not warm, fallback to model variant quantized (8-bit) to keep latencies up while warming
(we didn't attach the deck here, but the config doc is in the shared link)

16:02 Priya: can we control cache eviction? we have PII concerns and TTLs need to be short for some customers.
16:08 Carlos: yes, cache policies are per-route and per-tenant. TTL can be minutes to days, and we support explicit flush via API. for PII flows you can disable caching or enable encryption at rest with KMS keys.

18:30 Maya: quick demo screen-share (described verbally for transcript): carlos walked through the Optimize console, pointing to per-route token cost breakdown, the batching slider simulation, and a kv-cache hit-rate projection chart. we showed a small model of cost with toggles for hit-rate (30/50/70%) that updated the per-req compute tokens and monthly cost estimate.

21:45 Liam: that simulation is helpful. can we see actual numbers for a monthly projection? our volume is ~1M requests/day average, 80 rps peak.
21:52 Carlos: yes — rough back-of-envelope shown: baseline (no cache, modest batching) = 1.2k tokens * 1M req/day = 1.2 billion tokens/day. with our per-token compute $0.000012 => $14,400/day compute. With 60% cache hit and batching uplift, computed tokens drop to roughly 540 tokens/request => 540M tokens/day => $6,480/day. That's about 55% cost reduction in compute; combined with batching uplift on GPU efficiency we often see 3-4x reduction in billed inference cost vs naive baseline.
22:20 Priya: are those per-token numbers including overhead for KV cache indexing and storage costs?
22:26 Carlos: good qs — storage for cache (KV) is small relative to compute, typically a few dollars to low hundreds per month depending on size; the model above focuses on compute cost which dominates. indexing overhead adds negligible extra compute per request on hits; misses have the normal compute. we can share a spreadsheet with exact assumptions.

25:00 Liam: security checklist — we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS, and ability to run in our VPC.
25:10 Maya: all supported: SOC2 report available, SAML SSO for console, RBAC, audit logs per request available, KMS integration for key management, and Private deployment options (VPC or on-prem) for regulated tenants. we'll attach security pack.
25:22 Ethan: any compliance impact of KV cache? like does it store tokens that could be PII?
25:28 Carlos: only what you allow — cache can be disabled per-route and TTLs set to minimal. for PII routes we usually recommend disable or strict TTL + KMS. also audit logs show cache flush events.

28:10 Priya: on pilot scope — what's lightweight?
28:15 Maya: pilot approach: 2-week bench run + 4-week production pilot for a subset of traffic. Bench run: we run your representative workload on Dedicated trial pool to validate latency and cost model. Pilot: route 10-20% traffic to Redwood with monitoring. if results match thresholds we expand.
28:35 Liam: ok timeline wise we want to start bench in next week. is that realistic?
28:40 Carlos: yes — if you provide prompt sets + histograms by 2026-12-07 we can schedule bench next week, results within 2-3 days.

31:02 Maya: quick recap of open items and owners...
31:08 Maya: maya send pricing/SOW and security docs by 12/10; carlos schedule bench and share runbook by 12/09; liam share sample prompts by 12/07; schedule pilot kickoff week of 12/12.

32:50 Priya: small question on deployment mode — can we start on hosted and then move to Dedicated without major rework?
32:56 Carlos: yes — deployment abstraction is consistent: same API and route configs. you can pin model versions and move traffic to Dedicated pool via routing rules. we also support private control plane for full isolation if needed.

36:10 Liam: one last cost question — do you bill per computed token or per-request? we want to ensure predictable billing for finance team.
36:17 Maya: we do per-token compute for hosted usage; for Dedicated reserved capacity we offer committed throughput pricing (monthly commit) which makes finance forecasting simpler. we'll include both options in the pricing doc.

40:00 Ethan: ok great, that covered the big things. thanks.
40:05 Maya: thanks all. we'll follow up with the docs and schedule.

47:55 (call ends)
